changelog.change: Steps 4 and 5 are a stopwatch around each request, not the server's sum.
changelog.why: It follows item-health-row, where both columns are written.

changelog.change: Initial shape: one row an item, an offset, eight steps and the residual.
changelog.why: Contracts before logic - the writers and the chart need one fixed shape first.

description: One item's bar: where it starts on the run's clock, and what it spent.

extract_ms.description: Step 3. Taking the article out of the page, as the census spells it.
extract_ms.title: Extract Ms

fetch_ms.description: Step 2. Reading the page, as `ItemHealthRow.fetch_ms` spells it.
fetch_ms.title: Fetch Ms

item_id.description: The item this bar is about. An item no shard was given produces no row rather than an empty one, so an absent row reads as never worked.
item_id.title: Item Id

item_total_ms.description: How long the bar is - what the item cost once its wait is taken out, which is the same number `ItemHealthRow.item_total_ms` holds and spelled the same way. The wait is `start_offset_ms` and is drawn as position rather than length, so counting it here would draw it twice.
item_total_ms.title: Item Total Ms

label_ms.description: Step 4. The label call, on the stopwatch the census spells `label_ms`.
label_ms.title: Label Ms

plan_ms.description: Step 1. What choosing this item cost. Null where nothing timed it.
plan_ms.title: Plan Ms

publish_ms.description: Step 8. What placing this item in the day cost. Null where nothing timed it.
publish_ms.title: Publish Ms

residual_ms.description: `item_total_ms` minus the eight named steps: the part of the bar no step accounts for. Its own column because a step that absorbed the leftover reads as slower than it was. Signed on purpose - a negative value means two of the eight overlapped or two clocks disagreed, and the apportioned visual plan is a known overlap, so clamping it to zero would hide the one signal that says so. Derived here rather than supplied: a row that omits it gets it filled, and a row that disagrees with the arithmetic is refused.
residual_ms.title: Residual Ms

score_ms.description: Step 7. The model-free scorers, as `EvalRow.score_ms` spells it.
score_ms.title: Score Ms

shard.description: Which work shard read and summarised this item. Two bars overlapping on the clock is correct exactly when they sit on different shards, and without this column a reader cannot tell an overlap from a contradiction. The plan and publish steps are not sharded; this names the shard that did the middle.
shard.title: Shard

start_offset_ms.description: Milliseconds from the run's start to the moment this item's own work began. An offset and not a timestamp: the reader is asking where on the run's clock the bar sits, and an item that queued forty seconds has to sit forty seconds to the right for the queue to be visible at all.
start_offset_ms.title: Start Offset Ms

summary_ms.description: Step 5. The summarize-and-plan call, on the stopwatch the census spells `summary_ms`.
summary_ms.title: Summary Ms

visual_plan_ms.description: Step 6. What the visual plan cost. The plan is decoded inside the call above, so this is apportioned out of `summary_ms` rather than timed beside it - which is why the residual is signed.
visual_plan_ms.title: Visual Plan Ms
